english: Drug Accountability and Reconciliation
Issuing, counting, reconciling, storing and returning AZM bottles at the health facility.
Drug accountability and reconciliation in the health facility
Step — count and arrange AZM bottles in cartons for accountability.
OIC steps
OICs document AZM bottles received using the Issue and Receipt Voucher and the Inventory Control Card.
OICs issue the bottles each CDD team needs for its daily target, physically and in the technology app.
The number of bottles issued in the app must match the physical bottles issued.
All physical quantities issued to each CDD team are documented in the Inventory Control Card.
CDD team steps
Keep AZM bottles safely in the AZM bags provided, to avoid losses.
Reconstitute each bottle with exactly 15 ml of water.
Measure the exact dose shown on the app with the calibrated cups.
Capture any redosing for vomiting within 5 minutes in the app.
Finish each opened bottle before opening another.
End of day reconciliation
CDD teams separate empty bottles from unopened or unused bottles in the AZM bag.
The OIC counts each team's empty bottles and multiplies by 4. This gives the number of children to be reached.
The OIC compares this number with the children reached in the DIGIT HCM app.
Unopened plus empty bottles returned must equal the bottles issued that morning.
Storage and returns
Arrange empty and unopened bottles in separate cartons in the health facility.
Escalate all missing bottles to the LGA logistician and the NTD coordinator for investigation.
Return all AZM bottles (used and unused) in cartons to the LGA store within 3 days after implementation.

Key take away: drug accountability

CDD teams and OICs are responsible for AZM accountability at the health facility. Lack of accountability leads to pilferage and diversion of drugs into markets and drug sales outlets. Reconcile AZM and other commodities daily, at the end of the day. Arrange all used and unused bottles in cartons.
